correctness.rationale: An order-three character pushes normalized Haar measure to the uniform distribution on the cube roots of unity. For coefficients with |a|^2+|b|^2=1, the squared magnitudes are 1+r cos(phi+2 pi j/3), r=2|a||b| in [0,1]. Strict convexity and F(1,phi)>F(0,phi) force r=1. At r=1 their elementary symmetric functions are e1=3, e2=9/4, and e3=q=(1+cos(3 phi))/4. Differentiation of the roots of t^3-3t^2+(9/4)t-q makes the phase derivative s times the second divided difference of t^(s-1). Its sign is sign((s-1)(s-2)) for all real s=p/2>1. Endpoint triples (0,3/2,3/2) and (2,1/2,1/2) yield the sharp constants and exactly the stated phases. Finite checks are corroboration, not a proof of the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: The sharp Lambda(p) norm of a natural two-character Fourier span is a standard harmonic-analysis invariant. Exact order three is the first torsion setting where all real p>2 exhibit a genuinely nontrivial maximizing phase choice. The theorem gives the entire continuum of sharp norms and all extremizers and identifies a real phase reversal at p=4, which is neither a table lookup nor simply an interpolation of even moments. Scope is confined to two frequencies and exact relative order three.

limitations: Scope requires two distinct characters with relative order exactly three and every real p>2, not p<=2 or larger spectra.
Full author-hosted copy of a related independent Steinhaus/Orlicz source could not be read; only an abstract was available; originality remains best-of-knowledge.
An equivalent unindexed sharp three-vector Lp inequality or Banach-space statement remains a possible priority risk.
